claims.claim: .github/workflows/aios-self-hosted-wakeup.yml is dispatch-only and exposes only task_id and explicit codex/antigravity executor choice, with no untrusted triggers or arbitrary inputs.

The wakeup workflow strictly routes to [self-hosted, windows, x64, aios-renew], binds the persistent repository from AIOS_REPO_ROOT, performs no actions/checkout or worktree creation, and has no GitHub-hosted fallback.

Deterministic workflow contract regressions prove a successful wakeup invokes aios run exactly once with the dispatched TASK id, executor, and repository root, with no direct executor calls, duplicate AIOS invocations, manual git sync, or verification commands.

Workflow permissions are minimum read-only (contents: read) and no GitHub write token, PAT, deploy/SSH key, credential setup, checkout-persisted credential, or secret is injected into the AIOS or Executor process.

Deterministic workflow regressions prove missing repository binding, invalid git root, missing aios executable, or nonzero aios run outcome fails the job without retry, fallback, reroute, or success masking.
No files under src/aios_renew, existing tests, artifact schemas, or executor adapters are modified; A1 remains outer wakeup transport and preserves existing kernel and runtime boundaries.

README documents self-hosted runner prerequisites, AIOS_REPO_ROOT variable, workflow-dispatch invocation, non-interactive Git credential dependency, public-repository security boundary, and the fact that GitHub Actions wakes but does not replace AIOS Operator authority.

The canonical roadmap reconciles K0.4 as DONE, recognizes TASK-057..065 post-K0 hardening, maps TASK-063 to completed A8 Safe Publisher, maps A1 to TASK-066, and keeps remaining A-series items separately gated.
